s0003.literal: Emperor Xuan the Gaozong, taboo name Xu, style Shaoshi, childhood name Shili, was the second son of Prince Zhao-lie of Shixing.
s0003.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan the Gaozong, whose personal name was tabooed as Xu, who styled himself Shaoshi and in youth was called Shili, was the second son of Prince Zhao-lie of Shixing.

s0004.literal: He was born on xinyou day of the seventh month in the second year of Liang's Datong era, Editorial footnote marker 1. with red light filling the hall chamber.
s0004.idiomatic: He was born on xinyou day in the seventh month of the second year of Liang's Datong era (530). [1] Red light filled the hall.

s0005.literal: In youth he was broad-minded and possessed of many stratagems.
s0005.idiomatic: As a youth he was magnanimous and full of stratagem.

s0006.literal: When grown he was handsome in bearing; his body was eight feet three inches; his hands hung past his knees.
s0006.idiomatic: Grown, he was handsome, eight feet three inches tall, with hands that reached below his knees.

s0007.literal: He had courage and strength and was skilled at riding and archery.
s0007.idiomatic: He was strong and brave and skilled in horsemanship and archery.

s0008.literal: When the Founder pacified Hou Jing and garrisoned Jingkou, Emperor Yuan of Liang summoned the Founder's sons and nephews to attend court; the Founder sent Emperor Xuan to Jiangling, and by successive offices he rose to Straight Gate General and Secretariat Gentleman.
s0008.idiomatic: When the Founder crushed Hou Jing and held Jingkou, Emperor Yuan of Liang called the Founder's sons and nephews to court; the Founder sent Emperor Xuan to Jiangling, where he rose through posts to straight gate general and secretariat gentleman.

s0009.literal: At the time Horse Army Commander Li Zong was old friends with Emperor Xuan, Editorial footnote marker 2. and they often went about together. Emperor Xuan once lay drunk at night with lamps lit and slept; Zong had just gone out and soon returned, then saw Emperor Xuan's body was a great dragon; Zong was startled in terror and ran to avoid him in another room.
s0009.idiomatic: Horse army commander Li Zong was then an old companion of Emperor Xuan [2] and often kept his company. One night Emperor Xuan lay drunk with lamps burning; Zong stepped out and returned to find his body transformed into a great dragon. Terrified, Zong fled to another room.

s0010.literal: When Jiangling fell, Emperor Xuan was moved to the Guanxi region.
s0010.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell, Emperor Xuan was taken west to the Guan region.

s0011.literal: In the first year of Yongding he was enfeoffed by distant patent as Prince of Shixing commandery with a fief of two thousand households.
s0011.idiomatic: In Yongding year 1 (557) he received a distant patent as Prince of Shixing with a fief of two thousand households.

s0012.literal: In year three Emperor Wen succeeded to the throne and he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Ancheng.
s0012.idiomatic: In year 3, when Emperor Wen took the throne, he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Ancheng.

s0013.literal: In the third year of Tianjia he returned from Zhou and was appointed Palace Attendant, Secretariat Supervisor, Central Guard General, with aides and clerks.
s0013.idiomatic: In Tianjia year 3 (562) he returned from Northern Zhou and was made palace attendant, secretariat supervisor, and central guard general, with a full staff.

s0014.literal: Soon he was given the credential Staff of Office and made Area Commander over military affairs of the five provinces Yang, South Xu, East Yang, South Yu, and North Jiang, and Inspector of Yangzhou; his title was advanced to General of Agile Cavalry; the rest as before.
s0014.idiomatic: He was soon given the staff and made area commander over Yang, South Xu, East Yang, South Yu, and North Jiang, with the post of inspector of Yangzhou; he was promoted to general of agile cavalry, other offices unchanged.

s0015.literal: In year four he was given an establishment equal to the Three Dukes.
s0015.idiomatic: In year 4 he received a mansion equal to the three dukes.

s0016.literal: In year six he was transferred to Minister of Works.
s0016.idiomatic: In year 6 he was made minister of works.

s0017.literal: In the first year of Tiankang he was appointed Director of the Masters of Writing; the rest as before.
s0017.idiomatic: In Tiankang year 1 (566) he was appointed director of the Masters of Writing, other offices unchanged.

s0018.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, Emperor Xuan was appointed Minister of Education, advanced in title to Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Area Commander over all armies within and without, and granted thirty ceremonial swords.
s0018.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor ascended, Emperor Xuan became minister of education, was promoted to grand general of agile cavalry, made recorder of the Masters of Writing and commander of all armies at court and in the field, and was granted thirty ceremonial swords.

s0019.literal: In the first month of the second year of Guangda he was advanced to Grand Tutor, retaining the post of Minister of Education, with extraordinary honors, permission to wear sword and shoes in the hall, and his fief increased with the former to three thousand households; the rest as before.
s0019.idiomatic: In the first month of Guangda year 2 (567) he was made grand tutor while keeping the ministry of education, granted extraordinary honors and the right to wear sword and shoes in audience, and his fief was raised with the former total to three thousand households.

s0020.literal: On jiayin day of the eleventh month the Empress Dowager of Kind Instruction ordered the Deposed Emperor made Prince of Linhai and Emperor Xuan to enter the succession.
s0020.idiomatic: On jiayin day in the eleventh month the empress dowager of kind instruction deposed the emperor as Prince of Linhai and set Emperor Xuan to succeed.

s0021.literal: In the first month of spring, jiawu day, in the first year of Taijian, he took the throne in the Hall before the Supreme Ultimate and issued an edict: "When the sage receives the mandate and a king restores the dynasty, both rest on deep virtue before one becomes the primary consort.
s0021.idiomatic: On jiawu day in the first month of Taijian year 1 (569) he ascended the throne in the hall before the Supreme Ultimate and proclaimed: "Sages who receive the mandate and kings who restore a fallen house do so through deep virtue before they become sovereign.

s0022.literal: The Founder, the Martial Emperor, bowed to Yao's chart and wove Yu's tracks; his work matching Heaven shone on the stars and held to constancy; his merit reaching earth matched rivers and mountains in endurance.
s0022.idiomatic: The Founder, the Martial Emperor, took up Yao's design and continued Yu's work; his heaven-matching achievement lit the constellations and endured; his earth-reaching merit rivaled mountains and rivers in span.

s0023.literal: Emperor Wen embodied the utmost sage's form and met the age of martial virtue below; he built palaces to show frugality and sought only virtue; in setting the tripod's first base his purpose lay there.
s0023.idiomatic: Emperor Wen bore the form of the highest sage and met an age that called for force below; he built palaces to teach thrift and cared only for virtue; the founding of the dynasty was his aim.

s0024.literal: We, of meager worth, are not sage or worthy; from of old We have borne the former rule and were to transmit the bright fortune.
s0024.idiomatic: We are slight in merit and no sage; long We have carried the former design and were to pass on the bright mandate.

s0025.literal: Though We personally received instruction and kept to the borderlands in heart, chanting the high wind of the youngest son and thinking of the distant trust of the Prince of Chengyang, since the heir apparent succeeded the state and took the throne in rightful place, wrong ways were not few, yet We waited to hear that punishments might be set aside.
s0025.idiomatic: Though We were trained in person and meant to hold to our fief, singing of the youngest son's lofty withdrawal and of the Prince of Chengyang's distant entrustment, once the crown prince ruled in rightful seat We hoped wrong would fade and punishments fall still.

s0026.literal: Who could have thought the royal house ill-fated, with plots of disorder again and again, the heavenly steps hard and the precious calendar about to fall—yet looking up to the fine mandate, it has gathered on Our person.
s0026.idiomatic: We never thought the house so ill-starred, rebellion plotting step after step, the throne's path perilous and the calendar near collapse—yet heaven's charge has settled on Us.

s0027.literal: Our heart is firm and sure,
s0027.idiomatic: Our heart is firm and sure,

s0029.literal: firm in oath to azure Heaven, Editorial footnote marker 3. yet the host of ministers opened their plea and clamored together at Wei Bridge; the honored mother of culture hung her heart at Everlasting Joy; facing the seal and cord was not only the thrice refusal of Tang of Yin, and treading spring and winter was more than the five yieldings of the King of Dai.
s0029.idiomatic: See editorial note 3. sworn firm to heaven—yet ministers pressed Us at Wei Bridge; the empress dowager's heart hung on Everlasting Joy; to face the seal was more than King Tang's three refusals, and the seasons we crossed were more than the King of Dai's five yieldings.

s0030.literal: Now We reverently receive Heaven's writ and respectfully accept the secondary jade.
s0030.idiomatic: Now We reverently take Heaven's writ and accept the secondary jade.

s0031.literal: If We lean on the dark sea, Our dread and diligence only increase.
s0031.idiomatic: Standing on so vast a sea, Our dread and care only deepen.

s0032.literal: We think how clouds move and rain falls so all things prosper; We should share this with the black-haired people.
s0032.idiomatic: We mean to let cloud and rain pass so all things thrive and share this blessing with the people.

s0033.literal: Let Guangda year three be changed to Taijian year one.
s0033.idiomatic: Let Guangda year 3 be renamed Taijian year 1.

s0034.literal: A general amnesty is granted throughout the realm.
s0034.idiomatic: A general amnesty is proclaimed throughout the realm.

s0035.literal: Civil and military officials in office are each granted one rank; filial sons, dutiful brothers, and strong farmers, and those who are heirs to their fathers, are each granted one step of nobility; those of unusual rank and special talent are all to be advanced by examination.
s0035.idiomatic: Officials civil and military in post receive one step in rank; the filial, the dutiful, strong farmers, and heirs receive one step of nobility; men of rare talent are to be promoted by examination.

s0036.literal: Widowers, widows, orphans, and the solitary who cannot support themselves are each given five hu of grain.
s0036.idiomatic: Widowers, widows, orphans, and the destitute who cannot support themselves receive five hu of grain each.

s0037.literal: " The Grand Empress Dowager's honorific was restored to Empress Dowager.
s0037.idiomatic: " The grand empress dowager was again styled empress dowager.

s0038.literal: Consort Liu was established as empress; the heir Shubao as crown prince; the prince, South Center General and Inspector of Jiangzhou, Marquis of Kangle, Shuling, as Prince of Shixing to maintain Prince Zhao-lie's sacrifices.
s0038.idiomatic: Lady Liu was made empress; the heir Shubao crown prince; Prince Shuling of Kangle, south center general and inspector of Jiangzhou, was made Prince of Shixing to tend Prince Zhao-lie's shrine.

s0039.literal: On yiwei day the imperial carriage visited the imperial temple.
s0039.idiomatic: On yiwei day the emperor visited the ancestral temple.

s0040.literal: On dingyou day commissioners were separately appointed to tour the four quarters and observe local customs.
s0040.idiomatic: On dingyou day envoys were sent to tour the four quarters and inspect local customs.

s0041.literal: Campaign South Grand General, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, and newly appointed Central Pacifying Grand General Zhang Zhaoda was advanced in title to General of Chariots and Cavalry; newly appointed Central Army Grand General, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, and Inspector of South Xuzhou Chunyu Liang was made General Who Campaigns North; Garrison North General, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, Inspector of South Xuzhou, and newly appointed Garrison West General and Inspector of Yingzhou Huang Faqu was advanced in title to General Who Campaigns West; newly appointed Pacify South General, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, and Inspector of Xiangzhou Wu Mingche was advanced in title to General Who Garrisons South; Garrison East General, Inspector of Yangzhou, and Prince of Poyang Boshan was advanced in title to Central Guard General; Ministerial Aide Shen Qin became Left Ministerial Aide of the Masters of Writing; Minister of Revenue Wang Li became Right Ministerial Aide of the Masters of Writing; Protector General Shen Ke became General Who Garrisons South and Inspector of Guangzhou.
s0041.idiomatic: Zhang Zhaoda, campaign south grand general with a mansion equal to the three dukes and newly named central pacifying grand general, was promoted to general of chariots and cavalry; Chunyu Liang, central army grand general, inspector of South Xuzhou, was made general who campaigns north; Huang Faqu, garrison north general and inspector of South Xuzhou, newly garrison west general and inspector of Yingzhou, was promoted to general who campaigns west; Wu Mingche, newly pacify south general and inspector of Xiangzhou, was promoted to general who garrisons south; Boshan, Prince of Poyang, garrison east general and inspector of Yangzhou, was made central guard general; Shen Qin became left ministerial aide; Wang Li right ministerial aide; Shen Ke, protector general, became general who garrisons south and inspector of Guangzhou.

s0042.literal: Editorial footnote marker 4. On xinchou day the imperial carriage personally sacrificed at the southern suburb.
s0042.idiomatic: See editorial note 4. On xinchou day the emperor sacrificed in person at the southern suburb.

s0043.literal: On renyin day the prince, Marquis of Jian'an, Shuying, was made Manifest Grace General and Inspector of East Yangzhou and re-enfeoffed as Prince of Yuzhang.
s0043.idiomatic: On renyin day Prince Shuying of Jian'an was made manifest grace general and inspector of East Yangzhou and re-enfeoffed as Prince of Yuzhang.

s0044.literal: Marquis of Fengcheng Shujian was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Changsha.
s0044.idiomatic: Shujian, Marquis of Fengcheng, was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Changsha.

s0045.literal: On guimao day Bright Prestige General Zhou Hongzheng was made Special Grand Master.
s0045.idiomatic: On guimao day Zhou Hongzheng, bright prestige general, was made special grand master.

s0046.literal: On wuwu day the imperial carriage personally sacrificed at the imperial temple.
s0046.idiomatic: On wuwu day the emperor sacrificed in person at the ancestral temple.

s0047.literal: Second month, gengwu day: the empress visited the imperial temple.
s0047.idiomatic: On gengwu day in the second month the empress visited the ancestral temple.

s0048.literal: On xinwei day the crown prince visited the imperial temple.
s0048.idiomatic: On xinwei day the crown prince visited the ancestral temple.

s0049.literal: On yihai day the imperial carriage personally plowed the sacred field.
s0049.idiomatic: On yihai day the emperor plowed the sacred field in person.

s0050.literal: Summer, fifth month, jiawu day: Qi sent envoys on a friendly visit.
s0050.idiomatic: On jiawu day in the fifth month of summer Qi sent envoys on a friendly visit.

s0051.literal: On dingsi day Minister of Personnel and concurrent Grand Compiler Xu Ling was made Right Ministerial Aide of the Masters of Writing; Crown Prince Tutor and Commandant of Horse for the Consort Shen Junli was made Minister of Personnel.
s0051.idiomatic: On dingsi day Xu Ling, minister of personnel and grand compiler, became right ministerial aide; Shen Junli, crown prince tutor and commandant of horse for the consort, became minister of personnel.

s0052.literal: Autumn, seventh month, xinmao day: the crown prince received Lady Shen as consort; princes, dukes, and officials down were given silk gifts in varying measure.
s0052.idiomatic: On xinmao day in the seventh month of autumn the crown prince took Lady Shen; princes, nobles, and officials received silk in varying measure.

s0053.literal: On dingyou day Pacify East General and Administrator of Wu commandery, Prince of Jin'an Bongong, was made Central Protector and advanced in title to Pacify South General.
s0053.idiomatic: On dingyou day Bongong, Prince of Jin'an, pacify east general and administrator of Wu, was made central protector and promoted to pacify south general.

s0054.literal: Ninth month, jiachen day: the newly appointed Central Protector, Prince of Jin'an Bongong, was made Central Commandant.
s0054.idiomatic: On jiachen day in the ninth month Bongong, Prince of Jin'an and newly named central protector, was made central commandant.

s0055.literal: Winter, tenth month: the newly appointed Left Guard General Ouyang He seized Guangzhou and raised troops in rebellion.
s0055.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter Ouyang He, newly left guard general, seized Guangzhou and rebelled.

s0056.literal: On xinwei day General of Chariots and Cavalry, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, Zhang Zhaoda was sent leading the host to attack him.
s0056.idiomatic: On xinwei day Zhang Zhaoda, general of chariots and cavalry with a mansion equal to the three dukes, was sent with troops against him.

s0057.literal: On renwu day the imperial carriage personally sacrificed at the imperial temple.
s0057.idiomatic: On renwu day the emperor sacrificed in person at the ancestral temple.

s0058.literal: Spring, first month, yiyou day, in year two: Campaign West Grand General, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, and Inspector of Yingzhou Huang Faqu was made Central Authority Grand General.
s0058.idiomatic: On yiyou day in the first month of year 2 Huang Faqu, campaign west grand general and inspector of Yingzhou, was made central authority grand general.

s0059.literal: On jingwu day the imperial carriage personally sacrificed at the imperial temple.
s0059.idiomatic: On jingwu day the emperor sacrificed in person at the ancestral temple.

s0060.literal: Second month, guiwei day: Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes Zhang Zhaoda captured Ouyang He and sent him to the capital; he was beheaded in the Jiankang market; Guangzhou was pacified.
s0060.idiomatic: On guiwei day in the second month Zhang Zhaoda, equal in rank to the three dukes, seized Ouyang He and sent him to the capital; he was beheaded in the Jiankang market and Guangzhou was pacified.

s0061.literal: Third month, jingshen day: the empress dowager died.
s0061.idiomatic: On jingshen day in the third month the empress dowager died.

s0062.literal: On jingwu day a partial amnesty was granted to Guang and Heng provinces.
s0062.idiomatic: On jingwu day Guang and Heng provinces received a partial amnesty.

s0063.literal: On dingwei day a general amnesty was granted throughout the realm.
s0063.idiomatic: On dingwei day a general amnesty was proclaimed.

s0064.literal: Another edict said: "From the campaigns against Zhou Di and Hua Jiao onward, wherever arms had clashed and men died, all are to be gathered in and given coffins and sent back to their native districts;
s0064.idiomatic: A further edict said: "From the wars against Zhou Di and Hua Jiao onward, wherever battle killed men, their bodies are to be collected, coffined, and sent home;

s0065.literal: those whose wounds were not yet healed are each to be given medicine."
s0065.idiomatic: the wounded who are not yet healed are each to receive medicine."

s0066.literal: Summer, fourth month, yimao day: the Prince of Linhai Bozong died.
s0066.idiomatic: On yimao day in the fourth month of summer Bozong, Prince of Linhai, died.

s0067.literal: On wuyin day the empress dowager was buried beside the Wan'an tomb.
s0067.idiomatic: On wuyin day the empress dowager was buried at Wan'an.

s0068.literal: Intercalary month, wushen day: the imperial carriage visited the imperial temple.
s0068.idiomatic: On wushen day in the intercalary month the emperor visited the ancestral temple.

s0069.literal: On jiyou day the Metal Star appeared in daylight.
s0069.idiomatic: On jiyou day Venus was seen by day.

s0070.literal: Fifth month, yimao day: Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes Huang Faqu presented one auspicious jade disk.
s0070.idiomatic: On yimao day in the fifth month Huang Faqu, equal in rank to the three dukes, presented an auspicious jade disk.

s0071.literal: On renwu day Qi sent envoys to offer condolences.
s0071.idiomatic: On renwu day Qi sent envoys of condolence.

s0072.literal: Sixth month, wuzi day: Silla sent envoys presenting local products.
s0072.idiomatic: On wuzi day in the sixth month Silla sent tribute envoys.

s0073.literal: On xinmao day great hail fell.
s0073.idiomatic: On xinmao day heavy hail fell.

s0074.literal: On yisi day commissioners were separately sent to tour the provinces and commanderies and examine wrongful imprisonment.
s0074.idiomatic: On yisi day envoys were sent to tour provinces and commanderies and review unjust cases.

s0075.literal: On wushen day General of Chariots and Cavalry, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, Zhang Zhaoda was advanced in title to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry; Pacify South General and Inspector of Guangzhou Shen Ke was advanced in title to General Who Garrisons South.
s0075.idiomatic: On wushen day Zhang Zhaoda was promoted to grand general of chariots and cavalry; Shen Ke, pacify south general and inspector of Guangzhou, was promoted to general who garrisons south.

s0076.literal: Autumn, eighth month, jiashen day, an edict said: "Cherishing the distant through virtue is the constant rule; casting off the barbarian and drawing near to splendor is the people's root desire.
s0076.idiomatic: On jiashen day in the eighth month of autumn an edict said: "To cherish the distant through virtue is the constant way; to leave the barbarian garb and come to civilization is the people's deepest wish.

s0077.literal: In recent years along the Yangzi people have swaddled their infants and followed one another in hard journeys homeward; the frontier posts have never ceased; they should receive added care and comfort, answering their sincere hearts.
s0077.idiomatic: In recent years along the Yangzi families have carried infants on the long road home; frontier posts have never been still. They deserve added care to answer their sincerity.

s0078.literal: Those in the wild borderlands who pull themselves out, whether in the capital or in the various provinces and garrisons, without regard to distance, are all to be exempted from labor and tax.
s0078.idiomatic: All who have left the wild marches, whether in the capital or in provinces and garrisons, near or far, are exempt from labor and tax.

s0079.literal: If old territory is recovered and our invaded lands are returned, all are permitted to go home without any restriction.
s0079.idiomatic: If old lands are recovered and our lost ground restored, all may return home without limit.

s0080.literal: Prefects, administrators, and magistrates are clearly to distinguish and settle them; good fields and abandoned villages may be assigned as convenient.
s0080.idiomatic: Prefects, administrators, and magistrates are to sort them clearly and settle them on good fields or in abandoned villages as fit.

s0081.literal: If anyone still levies assessments, he is to be judged as disturbing the people.
s0081.idiomatic: Anyone who still levies assessments is to be punished as one who harries the people.

s0082.literal: " Another edict said: "The people are the state's root, set down in the canon; to govern the state and love the people is again the common teaching.
s0082.idiomatic: " Another edict said: "The people are the root of the state, written in the canon; to govern the realm and love the people is the common teaching.

s0083.literal: We hear court at dawn and cease at dusk, toiling when the sun slants, intending to spread gracious favor and drench the hundred millions.
s0083.idiomatic: We hold court from dawn till dusk and labor when the sun is low, meaning to spread grace over the millions.

s0084.literal: In the Liang season's end government and punishments were abandoned and lacking, statutes and guidelines slack and tangled, usurpers and bandits rose again and again, and corvée and tax levies were especially harsh and minute.
s0084.idiomatic: At the end of Liang law and punishment failed, statutes tangled, usurpers and robbers rose again and again, and corvée and tax were especially harsh.

s0085.literal: Great Chen holds the realm and rescues these remaining ills; destroying the violent and bringing peace to the black-haired people, We had no leisure to create reforms; as years flowed on it was about to become custom—if it is not loosened, nothing can be set right; Our evening fear and morning dread are like a headache.
s0085.idiomatic: Great Chen took the realm and rescued these ills; crushing violence and pacifying the people, We had no leisure to reform at once; years have nearly fixed the abuse into custom—unless We loosen it, nothing can stand; Our dread by night and day is like a sickness in the head.

s0086.literal: We think to begin from the lowly and slight, restrain Ourselves to aid the people; though the treasury is not yet full, how can the ruler alone be satisfied—now reductions may be made and the excessive removed, Editorial footnote marker 5. hoping it may stand forever as the fixed standard, simple and easy to follow.
s0086.idiomatic: We mean to begin humbly, restrain Ourselves to help the people; though the treasury is not full, how can the ruler alone be rich—let the heavy levies be cut and the worst removed [5], that a lasting, simple standard may stand.

s0087.literal: From now on, for corvée on fields, when flood or drought causes loss of harvest, it is to be reported at the locality and submitted upward for proportional reduction.
s0087.idiomatic: From now on, when flood or drought ruins the harvest, corvée on the fields is to be reported locally and remitted in proportion.

s0088.literal: Soldiers who reach sixty years are all permitted to return home.
s0088.idiomatic: Soldiers who reach sixty are all to be released.

s0089.literal: Skilled artisans who die on corvée and the aged and sick are not to be replaced by new levies.
s0089.idiomatic: Skilled artisans who die on corvée, and the aged and sick, are not to be replaced by new drafts.

s0090.literal: Those in the registers who hide skill, and princes, dukes, and all offices who rashly receive the people as tax shields, are to be returned to their original jurisdiction; an amnesty is granted for voluntary confession.
s0090.idiomatic: Hidden skilled men on the registers, and princes, nobles, and offices that take the people as tax shields, are to be returned to their proper rolls; voluntary confession is forgiven.

s0091.literal: Those in office handling affairs must in turn inspect and show one another; if loss is not reported, the office in charge bears guilt.
s0091.idiomatic: Officers in charge must inspect one another; failure to report loss makes the responsible office guilty.

s0092.literal: When magistrates and elders are replaced, they are to list in detail the households released from corvée and hand them to their successors for the revenue office.
s0092.idiomatic: When magistrates and elders are replaced, they must list households freed from corvée and deliver the list to their successors for the revenue office.

s0093.literal: If households increase, reward is added at once;
s0093.idiomatic: If households grow, promotion and reward follow at once;

s0094.literal: if they cause decrease and scattering, judgment follows the matter.
s0094.idiomatic: if they cause loss and flight, judgment follows the facts.

s0095.literal: Those who can open wasteland, without regard to few or many mou, are exempted from tax as before.
s0095.idiomatic: Whoever opens wasteland, whether many mou or few, is exempt from tax as before.

s0096.literal: " On wuzi day the Metal Star appeared in daylight.
s0096.idiomatic: " On wuzi day Venus was seen by day.

s0097.literal: Ninth month, yichou day: Regular Attendant, Garrison East General, and Administrator of Wuxing Du Ling was made Special Grand Master and Protector General.
s0097.idiomatic: On yichou day in the ninth month Du Ling, regular attendant, garrison east general, and administrator of Wuxing, was made special grand master and protector general.

s0098.literal: Winter, tenth month, yiyou day: the imperial carriage personally sacrificed at the imperial temple.
s0098.idiomatic: On yiyou day in the tenth month of winter the emperor sacrificed in person at the ancestral temple.

s0099.literal: Eleventh month, xinyou day: Goguryeo sent envoys presenting local products.
s0099.idiomatic: On xinyou day in the eleventh month Goguryeo sent tribute envoys.

s0100.literal: Twelfth month, guisi night: thunder sounded in the northwest.
s0100.idiomatic: On the night of guisi day in the twelfth month thunder sounded in the northwest.
